Comments (English): Media Dishwasher 6-person, MDW-601W (White), On-site installation Hello, this is Coupang reviewer Han Dae-ham. We are a newlywed couple in our second year, and we bought almost all of the home appliances except for the dishwasher when we got married. I thought we could do well as newlyweds even if we didn't buy the dishwasher. But it was very difficult to move into the house, have dinner, and wash the dishes. I think a dishwasher is essential for dual-income couples these days. That's how peace can exist in the family. This is a great product that can reduce the possibility of minor disputes. Although it is not built-in, if you live in a slightly older house or do not want separate construction, a 6-person dishwasher would be perfect because the size is not burdensome (I recently heard a review from a friend who is using a 12-person dishwasher. He said that a 2-person household does not use a lot of dishes, but it is too big to run the dishwasher on a 12-person unit and it is a burden and cannot be used properly!) As expected, the installation was very fast because it was Coupang installation. The installer was very kind and came on the desired date and gave a kind and thorough explanation, but the installer was not someone who appeared in the media, but someone who installs all the dishwashers on Coupang! So he told me that the user manual would explain it better than he did and told me to read it carefully. Still, he kindly did a good job of covering the basics. The components include a tray (including cup and spoon trays), an inlet hose, a drain hose, a washing blade, a filter, and a detergent inlet. In my house, the previous owner had already made a hole to use a water purifier, so I connected the inlet hose there and didn't make any more holes! One of the unique things about media dishwashers is that the drain hose has to come out. Since it's for 6 people, the drain hose is clearly visible, which is a bit disappointing in terms of interior design. I think that's why people use built-ins a lot. My new home was all about neatness. There's nothing I can do about it. I think it's a trade-off between effort and neatness. (The drain hose is thicker than I thought and is about 4 meters long, so I can cut it, but the technician said it's better not to cut it.) It can be adjusted in 7 ways! It seems good because you can set it to strong, standard, eco, glass, 90 minutes, fast, and automatic cleaning according to the situation ~ There is also a reservation system so you can run it at the desired time. One thing that is disappointing here is that the program icons are P1~7, so I am not used to it yet, so it is a bit disappointing! There is a detergent inlet inside, and I thought I could put liquid in it, but the user manual recommends putting powdered detergent, so I bought another dishwasher detergent. I was going to buy a dishwasher detergent in powder form, but the technician recommended an alum, so I looked into alum, and since it is for 6 people, I bought a compact 6-person alum dishwasher detergent. Other reviews said it doesn't dissolve well, but the detergent I bought is a foaming detergent, so it washes well without residue! There are also dishes that are not suitable for dishwashers, so please check and use them! (Wood, dishes and spoons that are weak to heat, iron materials that are prone to rust, glassware that is weak to heat, dishes that may discolor, small dishes that may fall off because they do not fit in the tray)! I recommend it! I recommend this to those who really need a dishwasher rather than for interior use, but who don't mind the price and want to use it for 2-3 people. *This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. Comments (English): Media Dishwasher 6-person, MDW-601W (White), On-site installation Hello, this is Coupang reviewer Han Dae-ham. We are a newlywed couple in our second year, and we bought almost all of the home appliances except for the dishwasher when we got married. I thought we could do well as newlyweds even if we didn't buy the dishwasher. But it was very difficult to move into the house, have dinner, and wash the dishes. I think a dishwasher is essential for dual-income couples these days. That's how peace can exist in the family. This is a great product that can reduce the possibility of minor disputes. Although it is not built-in, if you live in a slightly older house or do not want separate construction, a 6-person dishwasher would be perfect because the size is not burdensome (I recently heard a review from a friend who is using a 12-person dishwasher. He said that a 2-person household does not use a lot of dishes, but it is too big to run the dishwasher on a 12-person unit and it is a burden and cannot be used properly!) As expected, the installation was very fast because it was Coupang installation. The installer was very kind and came on the desired date and gave a kind and thorough explanation, but the installer was not someone who appeared in the media, but someone who installs all the dishwashers on Coupang! So he told me that the user manual would explain it better than he did and told me to read it carefully. Still, he kindly did a good job of covering the basics. The components include a tray (including cup and spoon trays), an inlet hose, a drain hose, a washing blade, a filter, and a detergent inlet. In my house, the previous owner had already made a hole to use a water purifier, so I connected the inlet hose there and didn't make any more holes! One of the unique things about media dishwashers is that the drain hose has to come out. Since it's for 6 people, the drain hose is clearly visible, which is a bit disappointing in terms of interior design. I think that's why people use built-ins a lot. My new home was all about neatness. There's nothing I can do about it. I think it's a trade-off between effort and neatness. (The drain hose is thicker than I thought and is about 4 meters long, so I can cut it, but the technician said it's better not to cut it.) It can be adjusted in 7 ways! It seems good because you can set it to strong, standard, eco, glass, 90 minutes, fast, and automatic cleaning according to the situation ~ There is also a reservation system so you can run it at the desired time. One thing that is disappointing here is that the program icons are P1~7, so I am not used to it yet, so it is a bit disappointing! There is a detergent inlet inside, and I thought I could put liquid in it, but the user manual recommends putting powdered detergent, so I bought another dishwasher detergent. I was going to buy a dishwasher detergent in powder form, but the technician recommended an alum, so I looked into alum, and since it is for 6 people, I bought a compact 6-person alum dishwasher detergent. Other reviews said it doesn't dissolve well, but the detergent I bought is a foaming detergent, so it washes well without residue! There are also dishes that are not suitable for dishwashers, so please check and use them! (Wood, dishes and spoons that are weak to heat, iron materials that are prone to rust, glassware that is weak to heat, dishes that may discolor, small dishes that may fall off because they do not fit in the tray)! I recommend it! I recommend this to those who really need a dishwasher rather than for interior use, but who don't mind the price and want to use it for 2-3 people. *This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. Sentence (English): This replaced a 30 year old Jenn Air that worked ok but I could no longer find parts for.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This replaced a 30 year old Jenn Air that worked ok but I could no longer find parts for. The first thing that became obvious is how quiet this Bosch dishwasher is. Like crazy quiet. You can easily stand in front of it while its running and have a completely normal conversation. I haven't tried the extra quiet mode setting on the app but I don't think I'll need to as it's already ridiculously quiet. It's inaudible from the next room. The only loud noise it really makes is when it drains the water really gurgles going down the drain. It's like it has a really strong drain pump that makes the water gurgle more than our old dishwasher. But it's not an issue as it only drains for a short interval a couple times each cycle. It does a great job cleaning, I usually just use the normal cycle for regular dishes and the auto cycle for dirtier loads. I usually select the extra dry setting from the app and most of the load comes out dry. I'm old school so I was a little put off at first about having to use my phone to select certain options but the app is fairly easy to use and works well. The main thing is that this dishwasher is quiet, works well and looks good too.

Sentence (English): 33 months.
Comments (English): 33 months. I turn it on once a day before going to bed. The difference in life when I didn’t have it and when I did is completely different. I have to wash the dishes even if I only drink a cup of coffee, and because it’s a hassle to wear gloves every time, I always washed the dishes with my bare hands, so my hands were always in a bad state because of the dishwashing detergent. I can’t stand seeing things that are messy in front of me, and I also have a cat, so I couldn’t just pile them up. When the dishwasher comes in, I just rinse it lightly with water and open the dishwasher right away and go to bed. I put it in the dishwasher and press it before going to bed. Since there are no dishes visible outside, the kitchen is much cleaner. Before, I had to look at the dishes here and there to dry them after washing them, but now I can’t see them anymore. It’s even better because they’re sterilized. People sometimes make mistakes when they wash dishes, so when I go to someone else’s house and go to a house with a dishwasher, I feel sanitary even when I eat something. Sentence (English): We have had the Bespoke dishwasher going on a little over a year.
Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY----- TERRIBLE PRODUCT ] || ---------------- || We have had the Bespoke dishwasher going on a little over a year. When we first got the dishwasher, it worked great, we absolutely loved it until we hated it. Months after having it, we started having problems with it not running properly. You would start a cycle, the dishwasher would run but it wasn't running with any water, just the motor ran. We would change the dishwasher settings to auto or just normal, and when we were lucky the dishwasher would run on normal storm wash setting. After reading many reviews, a lot of other people have had or have been having the same issues that we have been having with our dishwasher. I reached out to Samsung Care Support, which I have to say the customer service was good, considering I haven't heard good things about their customer service. We were given instructions to troubleshoot the dishwasher. We troubleshooted it, and we still continued to have the same issues. I reached back out to customer service to start a ticket for someone to come to my home and service the dishwasher. The gentleman that came out was helpful and honest with us, he said most likely that the repairs needed probably wouldn't be covered under the 5-year warranty. He diagnosed our dishwasher, the touch pad and the board inside the dishwasher went bad. To us, that is an electronic issue in the dishwasher hints (touch pad), to Samsung this is not an electronic issue, and therefore it is not covered under the 5-year warranty. After parts and labor, it would cost us more to fix the dishwasher than it cost us when we bought the dishwasher. with that being said we have no other choice but to buy a new dishwasher. It blows my mind that Samsung is allowed to sell such a terrible product on the market. I can't say it enough. DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY BUYING THIS DISHWASHER.

Sentence (English): I've been using it for 14 days.
Comments (English): [ Fully integrated dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I've been using it for 14 days. It's not my first Bosch. Before that, I had a very similar one, only an older version with fewer programs. Once a Bosch, always a Bosch! Honestly: even now, for the time being, I mainly use one or two programs, which are Auto and Express. I'm the only one in the household. When I have my family over for lunch during the holidays, I'll of course try another program. I'm interested in the Home Connect app, which connects the machine to your mobile phone. I've already downloaded and tested it. The delay start function allows me to set the start of the wash cycle for a more flexible schedule, which means I can program the time that suits me best, especially in terms of electricity costs. The built-in sensor programs adjust the electricity and water consumption depending on the degree of soiling of the dishes. The start time and the amount of dishes play a key role for me. Considering the brand, this machine is affordable. Of course, I don't know all the functions yet, because I haven't used them yet.
Comments (Original): [ Popolnoma vgradni pomivalni stroj ] || ---------------- || Uporabljam ga 14 dni. Ni moj prvi Bosch. Pred tem sem imela zelo podobnega, le starejšo verzijo z manj programi. Enkrat Bosch, vedno Bosch! Iskreno: tudi zdaj zaenkrat uporabljam v glavnem en ali dva programa, to sta Auto ter Express. Sem namreč sama v gospodinjstvu. Ko bom imela ob praznikih na kosilu družino, bom seveda preizkusila še kak drug program.Zanimiva mi je aplikacija Home Connect, ki ti s pomočjo mobilnega telefona poveže stroj. Sem jo že naložila in preizkusila.Funkcija zamika vklopa mi omogoča nastavitev začetka pomivanja za bolj prilagodljiv urnik, kar pomeni, da lahko programiram čas, ki mi najbolj ustreza, predvsem z vidika stroškov električne energije.Vgrajeni senzorski programi prilagodijo porabo električne energije in vode glede na stopnjo umazanosti posode. Čas vklopa in količina posode igrata pri meni ključno vlogo.Glede na blagovno znamko je ta stroj cenovno ugoden.Seveda še ne poznam vseh funkcij, ker jih še ne uporabljam.

Sentence (English): I finally understand why people say "new world, new world".
Comments (English): [ I bought it after much deliberation, but wow! ] || ---------------- || I finally understand why people say "Shinsegae, Shinsegae". I was surprised to see that the dishes were shinier than when I first bought them after washing them. I think I wiped them lightly because I'm not very strong with my hands. I prided myself on being careful not to leave any detergent residue behind, but now I realize my pride was misplaced. Furthermore, I skipped the salt and rinse, and there were no stains. The installer recommended adding dishwashing salt, so I did, but it didn't make a difference. They say tap water in Korea doesn't need it. Raising children and working, I'm always so busy that I don't have time to wear rubber gloves. I washed dishes by hand for over a decade. One day, I developed housewife's eczema. Whenever it seemed to get better, it would come back and itch in other areas. It's been years and years and hasn't gotten better, so I finally decided to buy this. The problem with a dishwasher wasn't the price itself, but the sheer magnitude of the installation. Four years ago, when we were remodeling, I should've added a dishwasher. Back then, I thought it was a luxury, so I skipped it. Over the years, I've developed eczema on my hands and my knuckles have gotten worse, and I regret it. Restaurant food is expensive, and with pre-cooked meals sold in bulk at supermarkets, I mostly eat at home, so there's always a lot of dishes to clean up. I need to clean up right away, but when I'm feeling good, I don't mind. But on days when I'm tired and exhausted, I wish someone else would do it for me. The day after I paid, an LG technician called and said he needed to inspect the property. The next day, a subcontractor set up the induction range, and the LG technicians installed it. Two people, one for two and a half hours. In my case, because my apartment wasn't as simple as a simple apartment, the additional cost was 221,000 won. It costs 150,000 won to turn on the induction stove, 30,000 won to cut the mop holder, 38,000 won to connect the water supply, and 3,000 won to dispose of the sink as district waste. The reasons I hesitated to install it were because it takes a long time to operate, it seems like double work to rinse and put the dirty dishes in, it's a hassle to install, and the electricity bill was a problem. I only run it once a day, and I hate having dishes pile up, so I bought a floating stainless steel dishwasher and soak it in the sink, and when it accumulates, I just throw it all in the dishwasher. I thought rinsing the food scraps would be a really tiring double work, but it doesn't feel like work as much as I thought. It's a 14-person stove, so it can hold all kinds of pots, medium, large, and small. I have more time to spend with the kids, and I have the energy to clean thoroughly, so the clutter at home is gone, and things are getting a little more organized. Today I'll clean out the fridge, tomorrow I'll organize the dresser, the day after that I'll clean the window frames, and so on. I'll just plan on doing the installation in half a day and save up for it. The electricity bill is probably due to the progressive rate, but I'm not sure since it hasn't come up yet. More important, I think, is resting my wrists. You don't know when you're young, but you get better with age. Conclusion: It seems essential for working moms who love raising children and cooking. When I was younger, I used to just wash dishes and laundry without thinking about my joints, but I ended up suffering from wrist problems and skin problems. I've been doing it once a day for about a month, and instead, I've been doing other chores like cleaning the bathroom, stairs, and organizing during the time I'd normally do the dishes. Thanks to this, my house is cleaner, and my eczema on my hands has completely cleared up. Today, I made kimchi and my back felt like it was going to break, but after throwing everything in the dishwasher and having a beer, I feel peaceful. It's especially great when I'm feeling under the weather and exhausted. The electricity bill is high for a four-person household, and it's around 70,000-80,000 won even in spring and fall, excluding winter and summer. I don't know if it's because of the dishwasher, or because I run the clothes dryer more, or because of the progressive rate system, but the water bill is lower, so I'll just ignore it.
Comments (Original): [ 오랜 고민끝에 구매했는데 헉! ] || ---------------- || 사람들이 신세계, 신세계하는 이유를 이제야 알겠어요.세척후 그릇이 처음 샀던 날보다도 더 번쩍번쩍 빛이나는 것을보고 놀랐어요. 평소에 손힘이 약하다는 이유로 슬쩍 닦았다는 생각이 드네요. 그래도 남들보다 오래오래 잔여 세제남기지않도록 신경써서 깨끗이 한다고 자부했건만 지금 와서 생각하니 잘못된 부심이었던 듯.게다가 소금과 린스는 생략했는데도 물때따윈 없네요.  설치기사님이 세척소금을 넣어주는게 좋다고하셔서 그 이후에는  넣어줬는데 유관상 안넣어도 차이는 없네요. 우리나라 수돗물은  안넣어도 된다고들 해요.  아이들키우며 맞벌이하느라 쫒기듯 살아서 고무장갑끼고 뺄 시간도 없어 맨 손으로 설거지를 십년이상 하니 어느날 주부습진이 한번 생기더니 나을만하면 다시 근질근질 다른 부분도 또 생겨 몇년째 반복하고 안 낫길래 큰맘먹고 구입하였네요. 식기세척기는 구매가격자체가 문제라기보다는 설치공사가 보통일이 아닐것같아서 엄두를 내기가 쉽지않았어요. 4년전 리모델링공사할때 세척기넣을껄 그때만해도 식세기는 사치품이다싶어 안했더니 몇 년새 손에 습진도 생기고 손가락 관절도 안좋아져 후회했어요. 식당음식값도 비싸고 마트등에서 대량으로 반조리식품들이 많이 나와 주로 집에서 먹으니 설거지거리는 항상 한가득인데 성격상 바로바로 치워야하는데 컨디션좋을때는 상관없지만 지치고 피곤한 날은 날은 누가 대신 해줬으면 싶더라고요. 결제다음날 엘지기사님 전화통화후 아무래도 현장 확인하셔야겠다고 오셔서 보시고 다음날 바로 인덕션 올리는 하청업체 직원분이 앵글올리고 앨지기사님들이 그 밑에 설치작업 두 분이  두시간반정도 하셨어요.저같은 경우에는 아파트처럼 단순구조가 아니여서 추가비용이 이십이만일천원들었네요.  인덕션올리는데 십오만원, 걸레받이자르는데 삼만원, 수도연결 삼만팔천원,  싱크장버리는데 구청폐기물 삼천원.설치를 망설였던 이유는 작동오래걸린다, 그릇 오염된것 찌꺼기 헹궈서 넣는것 이중 일인것 같다, 설치 귀찮다, 전기료 등의 문제였는데  하루 한번만 돌리는데 설거지거리 쌓아놓는것 싫어하는 사람인데 공중부양 스텐설거지통하나사서 개수대에 좀 담궈놓고 모이면 식기세척기에 다 때려넣어요. 음식물찌꺼기헹구는 것은 되게 피곤한 이중일일것같았는데 생각보다 일이라는 생각이 안드네요. 14인용이라 대중소 솥단지 다 들어가더라고요. 시간의 자유를 얻어 그 시간에 아이들과 보낼수도 있고  꼼꼼청소를 할 기운도 생겨 집에 묶은 때가 없어지고 정리정돈도 좀 되어가는 중이예요. 오늘은 냉장실정리, 내일은 서랍장정리, 그다음날은 창틀청소 등등 이런식으로.설치작업은 한나절만 작정하고 돈으로 싸바르면 되고 전기료는 생각하니 누진때문에그렇지 생각보단 안나온다던데 아직 안나와서 모르겠고  그것보다는 내손목관절과 휴식이 중요하다고 생각하면 되요. 젊을땐 몰라요. 나이드니 알게되네요.결론: 아이들키우고 요리하는것 좋아하는 직장맘은 필수인것같네요. 젊을땐 관절생각안하고 설거지, 빨래해댔는데 막썼더니  손목관절, 피부트러블이 생겨 고생해요.ㅡㅡㅡㅡㅡㅡㅡㅡ한 달정도 매일 한번씩 돌리고 대신 설거지할 시간동안 다른 집안일 욕실청소, 계단청소, 정리정돈등등 열심히 해서 집이 깨끗해졌고 손 습진이 싹 나았어요.  오늘은 김장하고 허리끊어질것같은데 식세기에 다 때려넣고 누워서 맥주 한 잔마시니 평화롭네요. 컨디션안좋고 쓰러질정도로 피곤할때 특히 너어무 좋네요. 전기료는 4인가구치고도 많 이써서 동,하절기 제외하고 봄가을에도 7-8만원은 나오는 집인데 식기세척기때문인지 빨래건조기를 더 돌려서 그런지 아님 구간 누진붙어서 그런지 1~2만원 더 나왔는데 대신 수도료가 덜 먹힌다니 그걸로 퉁칠래요.

I was surprised to see that the dishes were shinier than when I first bought them after washing them. I think I wiped them lightly because I'm not very strong with my hands. I prided myself on being careful not to leave any detergent residue behind, but now I realize my pride was misplaced. Furthermore, I skipped the salt and rinse, and there were no stains. The installer recommended adding dishwashing salt, so I did, but it didn't make a difference. They say tap water in Korea doesn't need it. Raising children and working, I'm always so busy that I don't have time to wear rubber gloves. I washed dishes by hand for over a decade. One day, I developed housewife's eczema. Whenever it seemed to get better, it would come back and itch in other areas. It's been years and years and hasn't gotten better, so I finally decided to buy this. The problem with a dishwasher wasn't the price itself, but the sheer magnitude of the installation. Four years ago, when we were remodeling, I should've added a dishwasher. Back then, I thought it was a luxury, so I skipped it. Over the years, I've developed eczema on my hands and my knuckles have gotten worse, and I regret it. Restaurant food is expensive, and with pre-cooked meals sold in bulk at supermarkets, I mostly eat at home, so there's always a lot of dishes to clean up. I need to clean up right away, but when I'm feeling good, I don't mind. But on days when I'm tired and exhausted, I wish someone else would do it for me. The day after I paid, an LG technician called and said he needed to inspect the property. The next day, a subcontractor set up the induction range, and the LG technicians installed it. Two people, one for two and a half hours. In my case, because my apartment wasn't as simple as a simple apartment, the additional cost was 221,000 won. It costs 150,000 won to turn on the induction stove, 30,000 won to cut the mop holder, 38,000 won to connect the water supply, and 3,000 won to dispose of the sink as district waste. The reasons I hesitated to install it were because it takes a long time to operate, it seems like double work to rinse and put the dirty dishes in, it's a hassle to install, and the electricity bill was a problem. I only run it once a day, and I hate having dishes pile up, so I bought a floating stainless steel dishwasher and soak it in the sink, and when it accumulates, I just throw it all in the dishwasher. I thought rinsing the food scraps would be a really tiring double work, but it doesn't feel like work as much as I thought. It's a 14-person stove, so it can hold all kinds of pots, medium, large, and small. I have more time to spend with the kids, and I have the energy to clean thoroughly, so the clutter at home is gone, and things are getting a little more organized. Today I'll clean out the fridge, tomorrow I'll organize the dresser, the day after that I'll clean the window frames, and so on. I'll just plan on doing the installation in half a day and save up for it. The electricity bill is probably due to the progressive rate, but I'm not sure since it hasn't come up yet. More important, I think, is resting my wrists. You don't know when you're young, but you get better with age. Conclusion: It seems essential for working moms who love raising children and cooking. When I was younger, I used to just wash dishes and laundry without thinking about my joints, but I ended up suffering from wrist problems and skin problems. I've been doing it once a day for about a month, and instead, I've been doing other chores like cleaning the bathroom, stairs, and organizing during the time I'd normally do the dishes. Thanks to this, my house is cleaner, and my eczema on my hands has completely cleared up. Today, I made kimchi and my back felt like it was going to break, but after throwing everything in the dishwasher and having a beer, I feel peaceful. It's especially great when I'm feeling under the weather and exhausted. The electricity bill is high for a four-person household, and it's around 70,000-80,000 won even in spring and fall, excluding winter and summer. I don't know if it's because of the dishwasher, or because I run the clothes dryer more, or because of the progressive rate system, but the water bill is lower, so I'll just ignore it.

Comments (English): [ I bought it after much deliberation, but wow! ] || ---------------- || I finally understand why people say "Shinsegae, Shinsegae". I was surprised to see that the dishes were shinier than when I first bought them after washing them. I think I wiped them lightly because I'm not very strong with my hands. I prided myself on being careful not to leave any detergent residue behind, but now I realize my pride was misplaced. Furthermore, I skipped the salt and rinse, and there were no stains. The installer recommended adding dishwashing salt, so I did, but it didn't make a difference. They say tap water in Korea doesn't need it. Raising children and working, I'm always so busy that I don't have time to wear rubber gloves. I washed dishes by hand for over a decade. One day, I developed housewife's eczema. Whenever it seemed to get better, it would come back and itch in other areas. It's been years and years and hasn't gotten better, so I finally decided to buy this. The problem with a dishwasher wasn't the price itself, but the sheer magnitude of the installation. Four years ago, when we were remodeling, I should've added a dishwasher. Back then, I thought it was a luxury, so I skipped it. Over the years, I've developed eczema on my hands and my knuckles have gotten worse, and I regret it. Restaurant food is expensive, and with pre-cooked meals sold in bulk at supermarkets, I mostly eat at home, so there's always a lot of dishes to clean up. I need to clean up right away, but when I'm feeling good, I don't mind. But on days when I'm tired and exhausted, I wish someone else would do it for me. The day after I paid, an LG technician called and said he needed to inspect the property. The next day, a subcontractor set up the induction range, and the LG technicians installed it. Two people, one for two and a half hours. In my case, because my apartment wasn't as simple as a simple apartment, the additional cost was 221,000 won. It costs 150,000 won to turn on the induction stove, 30,000 won to cut the mop holder, 38,000 won to connect the water supply, and 3,000 won to dispose of the sink as district waste. The reasons I hesitated to install it were because it takes a long time to operate, it seems like double work to rinse and put the dirty dishes in, it's a hassle to install, and the electricity bill was a problem. I only run it once a day, and I hate having dishes pile up, so I bought a floating stainless steel dishwasher and soak it in the sink, and when it accumulates, I just throw it all in the dishwasher. I thought rinsing the food scraps would be a really tiring double work, but it doesn't feel like work as much as I thought. It's a 14-person stove, so it can hold all kinds of pots, medium, large, and small. I have more time to spend with the kids, and I have the energy to clean thoroughly, so the clutter at home is gone, and things are getting a little more organized. Today I'll clean out the fridge, tomorrow I'll organize the dresser, the day after that I'll clean the window frames, and so on. I'll just plan on doing the installation in half a day and save up for it. The electricity bill is probably due to the progressive rate, but I'm not sure since it hasn't come up yet. More important, I think, is resting my wrists. You don't know when you're young, but you get better with age. Conclusion: It seems essential for working moms who love raising children and cooking. When I was younger, I used to just wash dishes and laundry without thinking about my joints, but I ended up suffering from wrist problems and skin problems. I've been doing it once a day for about a month, and instead, I've been doing other chores like cleaning the bathroom, stairs, and organizing during the time I'd normally do the dishes. Thanks to this, my house is cleaner, and my eczema on my hands has completely cleared up. Today, I made kimchi and my back felt like it was going to break, but after throwing everything in the dishwasher and having a beer, I feel peaceful. It's especially great when I'm feeling under the weather and exhausted. The electricity bill is high for a four-person household, and it's around 70,000-80,000 won even in spring and fall, excluding winter and summer. I don't know if it's because of the dishwasher, or because I run the clothes dryer more, or because of the progressive rate system, but the water bill is lower, so I'll just ignore it.

I was surprised to see that the dishes were shinier than when I first bought them after washing them. I think I wiped them lightly because I'm not very strong with my hands. I prided myself on being careful not to leave any detergent residue behind, but now I realize my pride was misplaced. Furthermore, I skipped the salt and rinse, and there were no stains. The installer recommended adding dishwashing salt, so I did, but it didn't make a difference. They say tap water in Korea doesn't need it. Raising children and working, I'm always so busy that I don't have time to wear rubber gloves. I washed dishes by hand for over a decade. One day, I developed housewife's eczema. Whenever it seemed to get better, it would come back and itch in other areas. It's been years and years and hasn't gotten better, so I finally decided to buy this. The problem with a dishwasher wasn't the price itself, but the sheer magnitude of the installation. Four years ago, when we were remodeling, I should've added a dishwasher. Back then, I thought it was a luxury, so I skipped it. Over the years, I've developed eczema on my hands and my knuckles have gotten worse, and I regret it. Restaurant food is expensive, and with pre-cooked meals sold in bulk at supermarkets, I mostly eat at home, so there's always a lot of dishes to clean up. I need to clean up right away, but when I'm feeling good, I don't mind. But on days when I'm tired and exhausted, I wish someone else would do it for me. The day after I paid, an LG technician called and said he needed to inspect the property. The next day, a subcontractor set up the induction range, and the LG technicians installed it. Two people, one for two and a half hours. In my case, because my apartment wasn't as simple as a simple apartment, the additional cost was 221,000 won. It costs 150,000 won to turn on the induction stove, 30,000 won to cut the mop holder, 38,000 won to connect the water supply, and 3,000 won to dispose of the sink as district waste. The reasons I hesitated to install it were because it takes a long time to operate, it seems like double work to rinse and put the dirty dishes in, it's a hassle to install, and the electricity bill was a problem. I only run it once a day, and I hate having dishes pile up, so I bought a floating stainless steel dishwasher and soak it in the sink, and when it accumulates, I just throw it all in the dishwasher. I thought rinsing the food scraps would be a really tiring double work, but it doesn't feel like work as much as I thought. It's a 14-person stove, so it can hold all kinds of pots, medium, large, and small. I have more time to spend with the kids, and I have the energy to clean thoroughly, so the clutter at home is gone, and things are getting a little more organized. Today I'll clean out the fridge, tomorrow I'll organize the dresser, the day after that I'll clean the window frames, and so on. I'll just plan on doing the installation in half a day and save up for it. The electricity bill is probably due to the progressive rate, but I'm not sure since it hasn't come up yet. More important, I think, is resting my wrists. You don't know when you're young, but you get better with age. Conclusion: It seems essential for working moms who love raising children and cooking. When I was younger, I used to just wash dishes and laundry without thinking about my joints, but I ended up suffering from wrist problems and skin problems. I've been doing it once a day for about a month, and instead, I've been doing other chores like cleaning the bathroom, stairs, and organizing during the time I'd normally do the dishes. Thanks to this, my house is cleaner, and my eczema on my hands has completely cleared up. Today, I made kimchi and my back felt like it was going to break, but after throwing everything in the dishwasher and having a beer, I feel peaceful. It's especially great when I'm feeling under the weather and exhausted. The electricity bill is high for a four-person household, and it's around 70,000-80,000 won even in spring and fall, excluding winter and summer. I don't know if it's because of the dishwasher, or because I run the clothes dryer more, or because of the progressive rate system, but the water bill is lower, so I'll just ignore it.

Two people, one for two and a half hours. In my case, because my apartment wasn't as simple as a simple apartment, the additional cost was 221,000 won. It costs 150,000 won to turn on the induction stove, 30,000 won to cut the mop holder, 38,000 won to connect the water supply, and 3,000 won to dispose of the sink as district waste. The reasons I hesitated to install it were because it takes a long time to operate, it seems like double work to rinse and put the dirty dishes in, it's a hassle to install, and the electricity bill was a problem. I only run it once a day, and I hate having dishes pile up, so I bought a floating stainless steel dishwasher and soak it in the sink, and when it accumulates, I just throw it all in the dishwasher. I thought rinsing the food scraps would be a really tiring double work, but it doesn't feel like work as much as I thought. It's a 14-person stove, so it can hold all kinds of pots, medium, large, and small. The electricity bill is high for a four-person household, and it's around 70,000-80,000 won even in spring and fall, excluding winter and summer. I don't know if it's because of the dishwasher, or because I run the clothes dryer more, or because of the progressive rate system, but the water bill is lower, so I'll just ignore it.

The installer recommended adding dishwashing salt, so I did, but it didn't make a difference. They say tap water in Korea doesn't need it. I've been busy raising children and working, so I haven't had time to wear rubber gloves. I've been washing dishes by hand for over a decade. One day, I developed housewife's eczema. Whenever it seemed to get better, it would come back and itch in other areas. It's been years and years, and it hasn't gotten better, so I finally decided to buy this. The problem with a dishwasher wasn't the price itself, but the sheer magnitude of the installation. Four years ago, when we were remodeling, I should've added a dishwasher. Back then, I thought it was a luxury, so I skipped it. Over the years, I've developed eczema on my hands and my knuckles have gotten worse, and I regret it. Restaurant food is expensive, and pre-cooked meals are often sold in bulk at supermarkets. I usually eat at home, so there's always a lot of dishes to clean up. I need to clean up right away, but when I'm feeling good, I don't mind. But on days when I'm tired and exhausted, I wish someone else would do it for me. The day after I paid, an LG technician called and said he needed to inspect the property. The next day, a subcontractor set up the induction range, and the LG technicians installed it. Two people, one for two and a half hours. In my case, because my apartment wasn't as simple as a simple apartment, the additional cost was 221,000 won. It costs 150,000 won to install an induction stove, 30,000 won to cut the mop holder, 38,000 won to connect the water supply, and 3,000 won to dispose of the sink as district waste. I hesitated to install it because it takes a long time to operate, it seems like double work to rinse and refill dirty dishes, it's a hassle to install, and the electricity bill were all issues. I only run it once a day, and I hate having dishes pile up, so I bought a floating stainless steel dishwasher and soak it in the sink. I thought rinsing food scraps would be a tiring double job, but it doesn't feel like work. It's a 14-person house, so it fits all kinds of pots, large, medium, and small. I have more free time to spend with my kids, and I also have the energy to do thorough cleaning, so the house is less cluttered and more organized. Today I'll clean the fridge, tomorrow I'll organize the drawers, the day after that I'll clean the window frames, and so on. The installation work is only half a day, so if you save money, you can save money. I think the electricity bill is probably because of the progressive rate, but I don't know because it hasn't come out yet. Rather, I think that my wrist joints and rest are important. You don't know when you're young, but you learn as you get older. Conclusion: It seems essential for working moms who like to raise children and cook. When I was young, I didn't think about my joints and just washed the dishes and laundry, but I ended up suffering from wrist joint problems and skin problems. I ran it once a day for about a month, and instead, I did other housework like cleaning the bathroom, cleaning the stairs, and organizing during the time I would have been washing the dishes. Thanks to this, my house is cleaner and my eczema on my hands has completely cleared up. Today, I made kimchi and my back felt like it was going to break, but I threw everything in the dishwasher, lay down, and had a beer, and it felt peaceful. It's especially great when I'm not in good condition and tired enough to collapse. The electricity bill is high for a four-person household, and it's around 70,000-80,000 won even in spring and fall, excluding winter and summer. I don't know if it's because of the dishwasher, or because I run the clothes dryer more, or because of the progressive rate system, but the water bill is lower, so I'll just ignore it.

I prided myself on being careful not to leave any detergent residue behind, but now I realize my pride was misplaced. Furthermore, I skipped the salt and rinse, and there were no stains. The installer recommended adding dishwashing salt, so I did, but it didn't make a difference. They say tap water in Korea doesn't need it. I've been busy raising children and working, so I haven't had time to wear rubber gloves. I've been washing dishes by hand for over a decade. One day, I developed housewife's eczema. Whenever it seemed to get better, it would come back and itch in other areas. It's been years and years, and it hasn't gotten better, so I finally decided to buy this. The problem with a dishwasher wasn't the price itself, but the sheer magnitude of the installation. Four years ago, when we were remodeling, I should've added a dishwasher. Back then, I thought it was a luxury, so I skipped it. Over the years, I've developed eczema on my hands and my knuckles have gotten worse, and I regret it. Restaurant food is expensive, and pre-cooked meals are often sold in bulk at supermarkets. I usually eat at home, so there's always a lot of dishes to clean up. I need to clean up right away, but when I'm feeling good, I don't mind. But on days when I'm tired and exhausted, I wish someone else would do it for me. The day after I paid, an LG technician called and said he needed to inspect the property. The next day, a subcontractor set up the induction range, and the LG technicians installed it. Two people, one for two and a half hours. In my case, because my apartment wasn't as simple as a simple apartment, the additional cost was 221,000 won. It costs 150,000 won to install an induction stove, 30,000 won to cut the mop holder, 38,000 won to connect the water supply, and 3,000 won to dispose of the sink as district waste. I hesitated to install it because it takes a long time to operate, it seems like double work to rinse and refill dirty dishes, it's a hassle to install, and the electricity bill were all issues. I only run it once a day, and I hate having dishes pile up, so I bought a floating stainless steel dishwasher and soak it in the sink. I thought rinsing food scraps would be a tiring double job, but it doesn't feel like work. It's a 14-person house, so it fits all kinds of pots, large, medium, and small. I have more free time to spend with my kids, and I also have the energy to do thorough cleaning, so the house is less cluttered and more organized. Today I'll clean the fridge, tomorrow I'll organize the drawers, the day after that I'll clean the window frames, and so on. The installation work is only half a day, so if you save money, you can save money. I think the electricity bill is probably because of the progressive rate, but I don't know because it hasn't come out yet. Rather, I think that my wrist joints and rest are important. You don't know when you're young, but you learn as you get older. Conclusion: It seems essential for working moms who like to raise children and cook. When I was young, I didn't think about my joints and just washed the dishes and laundry, but I ended up suffering from wrist joint problems and skin problems. I ran it once a day for about a month, and instead, I did other housework like cleaning the bathroom, cleaning the stairs, and organizing during the time I would have been washing the dishes. Thanks to this, my house is cleaner and my eczema on my hands has completely cleared up. Today, I made kimchi and my back felt like it was going to break, but I threw everything in the dishwasher, lay down, and had a beer, and it felt peaceful. It's especially great when I'm not in good condition and tired enough to collapse. The electricity bill is high for a four-person household, and it's around 70,000-80,000 won even in spring and fall, excluding winter and summer. I don't know if it's because of the dishwasher, or because I run the clothes dryer more, or because of the progressive rate system, but the water bill is lower, so I'll just ignore it.

Sentence (English): We've had our Bosch 800 dishwasher for a few months now.
Comments (English): [ Bosch dishwasher lives up to its reputation ] || ---------------- || We've had our Bosch 800 dishwasher for a few months now. Originally we had planned to purchase a Whirlpool, but after seeing and touching both machines in person, we went w/ the Bosch and have been very happy with our decision. The Bosch is extremely quiet, easy to load, holds a lot of dirty dishes, cleans extremely well and lives up to the Bosch dishwasher reputation. The 3rd flexible rack is great for flatware -- if you group like items, it makes for a very quick unload -- and is also perfect for washing small dipping dishes. The Bosch 800 is a very tall dishwasher so make sure to measure your space. The stainless steel front is more of a "whitish" (vs. gray) stainless steel. It does show water spots pretty easily, but also wipes up pretty easily w/ just a soft, wet cloth. And two minor things we don't love are 1) the angle and spacing of the tines on the front of the bottom rack is a bit awkward, and 2) that it doesn't seem possible to add the crystal dry cycle on to a quick wash setting (but we need to do some more research on this). Overall an excellent dishwasher that has made day-to-day life easier and that we would highly recommend.

Comments (Original): [ 이걸 왜 이제야 샀을까? 삶의 질 수직상승템 ] || ---------------- || ■ 구매시기 2022.11. 5.(토)  ■ 설치시기 및 과정 2022.11. 10.(목) 식기세척기는 먼저 빌트인장을 짜주시는 기사님을 만나 장을 짠 후 식기세척기 배달 및 설치기사님이 다음날 배달설치를 해주십니다. 일정이 잘 맞으면 다음날 바로 가능하지만 저 같은 경우는 일정이 맞지 않아 조금 시간이 걸렸습니다. 하지만 역시 언제나 쿠팡의 로켓설치는 진리입니다.  기사님은 정말 착하셨습니다. 장을 짜주시는 기사님은 오셔서 먼저 원하는 위치가 있는지 물어보시고 그 위치에 최대한 맞게 해주려고 하십니다. 저희 집은 12평에 좁은 집이어서 조금 애를 먹었습니다. 제가 장 위치를 3번 정도 변경했는데 그럼에도 짜증 한번 내지 않고 친절하게 진행해 주신 기억이 있네요^^ 장을 들어내고 그 위치에 맞게 들어가면 상관없지만 장을 짜야 되는 경우 추가금이 생길 수 있으니 참고하시기 바랍니다. 좁은 집에 빌트인으로 깔끔하게 넣고 싶었는데 너무 예쁩니다^^ ■ 구매이유  혼자 살지만 집에서 자주 해 먹는 편입니다. 그렇기 때문에 설거지거리도 많이 나옵니다. 바로바로 설거지하는 타입은 아니라 금방 쌓입니다. 집을 매매한 뒤로 삶의 질을 올리기 위해 가전제품을  많이 구입하려고 했습니다. 식기세척기도 그 중 하나입니다. 다들 식세기이모님이라는데 저도 한번 그 이모님 영접해보고 싶었습니다 ㅎㅎ  ■ 제품기능 및 성능 결론부터 말하자면 정말 깨끗하게 세척됩니다. 기름기가 묻은 그릇부터, 굳은 밥풀까지 \'뽀득\'느낌이 나게 세척됩니다. 기본적으로 그릇을 뒤집어서 놔야 합니다.  12인용이 있고 8인용이 있지만 저는 1인가구여서 8인용으로 주문했습니다. 저도 계속 사용하고 있는 중이어서 쓸 때마다 새롭게 알아가는 부분도 있어서 즐겁습니다.  소음: 소음은 없을 수 없습니다. 안에서 강력하게 물을 뿜어내고 있으니까요. 하지만 그 부분이 정말 크지 않아서 신경 써서 듣지 않으면 인지하지 못할 정도입니다. 리뷰를 보면 드라마틱한 설거지를 기대하지 마라고 돼있는데 저는 오히려 반대입니다. 기대를 안 했는데 드라마틱한 설거지가 돼있어서 너무나 좋습니다. 날마다 손에 물 묻히고 설거지하시는 주부에게 정말 식세기는 [필수]가 아닐까 싶습니다. 자동코스를 해놓으면 오염도에 따라서 알아서 설정됩니다. 공간: 앞서 말했듯이 저는 8인용을 주문했습니다. 어째서 8인용인지는 모르겠습니다.  그릇을 기준으로 한거 같습니다만 냄비나 프라이팬 같은걸 넣으면 공간이 쪼금 부족합니다. 참고하시기 바랍니다. 6개의 코스가 있으며 옵션으로 4가지가 있습니다. 더욱더 깨끗하게 원한다면 저처럼 스팀불림과 고온살균을 누르시면 되겠습니다. 설거지가 끝나면 문이 위 사진과 같이 알아서 열립니다.  내외부 공기가 순환되면서 건조의 효율을 높이기 위한 기능이라고 합니다. 문을 아래로 내리면 세제 투입구가 있는데 왼쪽은 고체형세제투입구 오른쪽은 식기세척기용 린스투입구입니다. 큰그릇들도 여유있게 들어가기는 합니다.  저도 정확히 파악을 하지 못해 어떻게 쌓아야 잘 세척이 되는지 파악중이지만 저렇게 놔둬도 정말 깨끗하게 세척이 되는게 신기할 따름입니다.  1층에는 집기류 및 수저, 젓가락을 넣을 수 있는 통이 있습니다. 2층은 컵이나 와인잔도 넣을 수 있도록 왼쪽에 틀?같은게 있습니다.  뒤짚어 놓다보니 위쪽 웅덩이같은 것에 물이 고이는건 어쩔 수 없는 것 같습니다. ■ 아쉬운점 아쉬운점이라 하면은 세제를 주지 않습니다. 미리 식세기용 세제를 구매해야 합니다. 그리고 구매하면 식세기전용 30% 할인 쿠폰을 줍니다.  그외 식세기로서의 기능은 120% 만족합니다. ■ 총평 - 삶의 질을 올려주는 필수템 1순위! - 애벌하고 식세기를 돌리라고 하지만 그러지 않아도 되는 강력함 - 고온세척으로 깨끗한 세척 가능 - 다양한 코스 옵션 - 쿠팡을 통한 빠른 로켓설치 가능 - 빌트인으로 자연스럽게 녹아드는 예쁜 디자인 - 세제나 린스를 미리 구입해야하는 아쉬움 - 왜 이제야 샀는지 모르겠네요 진짜 너무 편합니다.  구매후기가 도움이 됐다면 아래에  도움이 돼요 버튼 눌러주시면 감사하겠습니다^^

Comments (English): [ Works for us ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher was to replace a previous ASKO dishwasher that we had for 15 years. It comes with a few innovations, namely the electronic display panel and door open when the drying phase is reached. We paid for installation and the serviceman had preset the dishwasher to ECO, which was what we would have chosen if setting it ourselves. The dishwasher works well however our previous one held 12 place settings and had larger spaces for crockery. This one holds 14 place settings in the same size dishwasher so everything is squashed together more closely. Result is occasionally an item is not washed as well as it could be. Otherwise it works exactly as we expected. However the door open feature does not replace a drying cycle. Everything comes out damp even with a full rinse aid well. Luckily we only run it once a day and can leave the dishwasher for 24 hours for everything to dry.

Comments (English): #EventParticipation. Most of my acquaintances who use dishwashers are so satisfied that I wondered if I should buy a dishwasher. I hesitated for a while. I kept putting it off, but now that I have a child in my family of two, I feel like I have less and less time, and I keep putting off washing dishes, so I decided to buy a dishwasher in a hurry! Sentence (English): We originally bought an LG dishwasher to replace our very old Ikea unit.
Comments (English): [ A dishwasher that also dries the dishes ] || ---------------- || We originally bought an LG dishwasher to replace our very old Ikea unit. Having used dishwashers for decades, we were accustomed to opening the door at the end of the cycle to find dry dishes. The LG was incapable of drying the dishes, even with the extended drying cycles. A number of calls to LG eventually revealed that many new dishwashers do not include a heating element to perform the drying function, in an effort to gain a better energy efficiency rating. When the Best Buy guy came to check the unit, to make sure it was working properly, he confirmed that it was operation according to spec, and recommended we look at Whirlpool dishwashers. We returned to Best Buy to ask for an exchange. The Whirlpool performs as expected, and we don't have to towel-dry dishes anymore. Another thing we like about the Whirlpool is the reduced options for cycles; it has half the number of the LG yet performs perfectly well.

Sentence (English): In use for over a month and very satisfied.
Comments (English): [ Excellent dishwasher from BOSCH ] || ---------------- || In use for over a month and very satisfied. Sufficient space for all dishes and cutlery. Operation is easy, dishes come out nice and clean and dry. Door closes smoothly and everything is easy and good to put away. We had a cutlery basket with the old Bosch dishwasher, but now a cutlery drawer. This requires a bit more precision when putting away, but when taking out, sorting is no longer necessary. Our cutlery drawer in the kitchen is close to the dishwasher, but if it were further away, the basket might be more convenient, because you can take it out and take it to the cupboard. So far, mainly used 2 programs, both of which delivered good results. With ECO, the door opens at the end. Moisture then enters the living room. We use this setting to run at night. ECO takes longer, but is more economical. With auto, the door remains closed and is dried with zeolite. The dishwasher is very quiet. There are many more options, but we still have to try them out. We probably won't use Home Connect.
Comments (Original): [ Uitstekende vaatwasser van BOSCH ] || ---------------- || Ruim 1 maand in gebruik en heel tevreden. Voldoende ruimte voor alle servies en bestek. Bediening is makkelijk, vaat komt er goed schoon en droog uit. Deur sluit soepel en alles is makkelijk en goed in te ruimen. We hadden bij de oude Bosch vaatwasser een bestekmandje, maar nu een besteklade. Dit vereist bij het inruimen wat meer precisie, maar bij het uitruimen is sortering niet meer nodig, Onze besteklade in de keuken is vlak bij de vaatwasser, maar zou die verder weg zijn dan is het mandje misschien handiger, omdat je die eruit kunt halen en meenemen naar de kast. Tot nu toe hoofdzakelijk 2 programma's gebruikt die beiden een goed resulaat leverde. Bij ECO gaat de deur open aan het eind. Vocht komt dan in de huiskamer. Deze stand gebruiken we om 's nachts te laten draaien. ECO duurt langer, maar is zuiniger. Bij auto blijft de deur dicht en wordt gedroogd met zeoliet. De vaatwasser is erg stil. Er zitten nog veel meer mogelijkheden op, maar die moeten we nog uitproberen. Home Connect gaan we waarschijnlijk niet gebruiken.

Comments (English): [ GENIAL!  ] || ---------------- || I bought the appliance a month ago, and I preferred to wait a while so that my opinion could be as objective as possible. In general my assessment is very positive. This is the second 45cm dishwasher I have had. (The previous one lasted me 20 years, and I doubt very much that it will last that long). And therefore, I already know the pros and cons of the size not being that of a standard 60cm one. The main problem of course is the capacity that the appliance may or may not have. And in this case I have to admit that this is precisely what is most successful. All the spaces are usable, and the cutlery tray on the top is partly to blame for this being the case. So in that aspect I am very happy. It works, it is quite silent and that is also appreciated. It is programmable, something that my previous dishwasher lacked. Which is very interesting to take advantage of the hours of lower consumption. It also comes with its corresponding app, which I suppose there will be people who may find very useful. Although I think I will never use it. But it's good that this possibility exists. The dishwasher is fully integrated, and knowing all the assembly problems that this could entail, I bought it anyway. If the "IKEA" manuals may seem complex to you, I can assure you that compared to these, they are nothing but a joke. It is well indicated. But it is to be taken very slowly. So I hope to be able to assemble it in the next few days. I do not want this to be a problem for making the final decision not to buy it, since it is a product that I recommend 100%.

Honestly, this is not a bad compromise for the quietness, large size, and general optimization of this product. I would highly recommend this to any consumer!

Sentence (English): BLUF: Works perfectly.
Comments (English): [ This thing rocks! ] || ---------------- || BLUF: Works perfectly. It actually cleans and drys my dishes *exactly* like it's supposed to and the adjustable racks are genius. I finally bought this to replace the terrible cheap unit the previous homeowner put in after I got tired of fixing it, and the difference in build quality and function is night and day. Of course, I also discovered a slow leak in the plumbing under my kitchen sink in the process, but that isn't the dishwasher's fault and catching it now probably saved me from a disaster down the road. I recommend installing a hammer arresting device because the solenoid valve opens and shuts very quickly and can cause banging in the pipes, probably the cause of my leak-- again, not the new dishwasher's fault. I've been using the recommended Finish detergent and jet dry and things come out perfectly clean and dry every time. I trust that the sanitize cycle actually works in this unit because it definitely gets hot enough to melt and warp plastic even on the top rack, so be careful and check that it is marked as dishwasher safe-- again, not a flaw in the machine at all! This was me testing whether the items were actually dishwasher safe or not. On the previous unit I never bothered with plastic anyway because it never came out clean or dry. My whole workflow is better now. Everything goes in the dishwasher by default except for high carbon steel knives which would rust. Before, I only used the dishwasher for ceramic, glass, and stainless utensils, and even then did a significant amount of pre-handwashing myself. Now, dirty dishes go directly in the night before, clean dry ones come out the next morning. Amazing.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher had rave reviews.
Comments (English): [ Bosch dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher had rave reviews. We bought this model, not the top of the line, but the one under it. The features between the two seemed inconsequential and the savings was $500.00. It cleans the dishes and silverware beautifully. However, the configuration on the top shelf is very disappointing. It does not leave room for more than a few glasses and the bowls that we have do not fit in, either on the top or bottom shelf. The third shelf on top is not long or wide enough to put long items, like tongs. The silverware rack at the bottom is compartmentalized, but not large enough to put in butter knives or dinner forks. Also, if I do get them in, they are difficult to take out. I opened the top of the silverware rack and put the silverware in loosely, but that did not give it as thorough a wash. Overall, I am very disappointed after reading wonderful reviews. I would not recommend this particular model.

Sentence (English): The built-in Samsung dishwasher door broke, and when I called Samsung A/S, they said they couldn't fix it, so I had no choice but to purchase a new one.
Comments (English): [ Demolition must be done by the consumer. ] || ---------------- || The built-in Samsung dishwasher door broke, and when I called Samsung A/S, they said they couldn't fix it, so I had no choice but to purchase a new one. It was really convenient that I could confirm/change the delivery schedule through KakaoTalk notifications with just one or two clicks instead of having to wait for the delivery person to call me every time! On the other hand, the unexpected removal of the existing product was a big problem. The first remodeling technician who visited told me that the customer had to remove the existing product (cut off the line, cut off the water supply, etc.) first before installing the product. I had to block the hot and cold water pipes coming from the back wall, block the drain pipe, and cut off the electric line. I wondered if it was possible for the customer to do this himself, so I thought it would be right for Samsung to do it together with the installation, but the product installation was delayed for a week due to the delivery company and Samsung Service Center's evasion of responsibility and several arguments. In the end, I bought the parts myself at a hardware store and asked the management office's facility team to do the work, but it was not an easy process because there was a risk of water leakage. Since the Samsung product I was using was beyond repair, I had no choice but to replace it with a Samsung product. However, Samsung was stubborn and only wanted to collect the old product’s discarded home appliances and absolutely refused to get involved in the demolition work, which was very disconcerting from the consumer’s perspective. After going through many twists and turns, I finally got around to installing it, but it was an inconvenient and difficult experience in many ways.
Comments (Original): [ 철거는 소비자가 직접해야함 ] || ---------------- || 기존에 빌트인된 삼성 식기세척기 도어가 고장났는데, 삼성 A/S를 불렀더니 못고친다하여 어쩔수 없이 신규구매를 진행했습니다. 카톡알림을 통한 배송일정 확정/변경은 일일이 배송기사의 전화를 기다릴 필요가 없이 클릭 한두번으로 처리되는점이  정말 편리했어요!  반면 예상치도 못한 기존제품 철거가 큰 문제였습니다.  최초 방문한 리폼기사님께서 기존제품 철거작업을(단선, 단수 등) 소비자가 직접  선행해야 이후에 제품설치가 가능하다고 안내해주셨어요. 기존에 후면 벽으로부터 나온 온수, 냉수 수도관을 막아야하고 배수관도 막고, 전기선도 단선작업이 필요한 상황이었습니다.  이걸 소비자가 직접 하는게 가능한가 싶어서 삼성측에서 설치시 같이 작업해주는게 맞다고 생각했는데, 배송업체와 삼성서비스센터와의 책임 미루기 및 몇차례 실랑이로 일주일이나 제품설치가 미뤄졌어요. 결국 철물점에서 제가 부품들을 직접 사다가 관리사무소 시설팀 직원분께 부탁드려서 겨우 작업을 진행했는데, 누수 우려가 있는 작업이라 쉽지 않은 과정이었습니다. 사용중이던 삼성 제품이 수리가 불가하니 불가피하게 삼성->삼성 제품으로 교체를 한건데, 삼성에서는 기존 제품의 폐가전 수거만 해줄뿐 철거작업에는 절대로 개입하지 않으려는 완고한 태도였기에 소비자 입장에서 무척 당황스러웠습니다.  우여곡절 끝에 설치는 했는데 여러모로 불편하고 고생 많은 경험이었습니다.

Sentence (English): I'm extremely satisfied with the performance!
Comments (English): I'm extremely satisfied with the performance! Installation is a hit or miss with the technician. Since I received a Bespoke dishwasher as a gift, I decided to choose the Bespoke dishwasher in the same color rather than researching other brands! The price went up by about 30,000 won in just a few days since I had it in my cart, so I held back tears and just bought it. I debated for a few days; I should have just bought it and used it right away! It's my first time using a dishwasher, and I'm very satisfied. It cleans greasy food well and leaves everything squeaky clean. However, the installation was a problem. The technician opened the base cabinet like that to do something, then said he couldn't put it in because the sink had sagged, and just left. I wrestled with it for a long time to get it back in. Rocket Installation is great, but I've had it installed three times since moving, and the technicians were disappointing all three times. The product itself, though, haha.

Sentence (English): We purchased this dishwasher to replace our six-year-old KitchenAid, which had started leaking.
Comments (English): [ Quietly Gets the Job Done ] || ---------------- || We purchased this dishwasher to replace our six-year-old KitchenAid, which had started leaking. Fortunately, I had a water sensor underneath it that detected the leak before any damage occurred. After experiencing a significant fridge leak that caused major damage about 10 months ago, I'm extra cautious about water issues. That's why the AquaStop feature on this unit was a crucial factor in our decision. The dishwasher is encased in its own tub, designed to catch any leaked water, and automatically shuts off with an error code if it detects a leak or an irregular water flow. My dad has a similar Bosch model that alerted him to a leak, and a friend had a similar experience, so we knew this feature was essential for us. Note that not all models have this feature. Beyond the leak protection, this dishwasher is impressively quiet. It even has a laser light that projects onto the floor, indicating when it's running. We configured the unit to pop the door open for air drying at the end of the cycle, which isn't the default setting but has worked well for us. Since we run it overnight, the dishes are dry by morning. Of course, if items are positioned in a way that traps water, they may still be wet but we've experienced our plates and cups coming out dry. Occasionally, some coffee cups with cupped bottoms and plastic containers need a bit more drying, but we just place them on a drying mat. We didn't think it was worth spending an extra $400 on a model with the air-dry feature using sealed crystals, though it's a neat concept. At first, I was unsure about the door automatically popping open, but I've come to appreciate it. We were initially worried about the smaller silverware basket, as our previous dishwasher had a much larger one, but it hasn't been a problem. In fact, the smaller basket has freed up more space for larger items like pots and pans. We also find the top "third" rack handy for utensils and small items. To adjust certain features, such as the door opening, you'll need the app, which requires connecting the dishwasher to your home WiFi. It has remote start if you enable it, though I can't fathom why anybody would ever use that. Overall, the dishwasher is quiet, stylish, and does an excellent job cleaning. We also appreciate that it has no visible logo, making it easy to match with other appliances in the kitchen.

Sentence (English): This LG is very quiet compared to our previous "quiet" unit.
Comments (English): [ A new dishwasher after 28 years! ] || ---------------- || This LG is very quiet compared to our previous "quiet" unit. The top rack is functional for silverware and the middle rack is adjustable up or down. This Energy Star unit takes a bit longer to operate a cycle, but it does wash fine. Drying is good but being energy efficient, not super hot or fast. OK. The install, OMG, with front connections the lines and cords need to be extra LONG and you have to be a magician to keep from running them over as you back in the unit. Be aware of this as many standard install kits won't have long enough items. Front connections may seem like a neat thing but they are a pain. One star off for that design flaw. The bottom front panel is adjustable to flush up with the floor for a clean install look. Unit comes packages extremely well. Operational features are nice with front facing controls. No need to open the door to get to control panel. Lower silverware tray is redundant to upper rack and has been removed to make more room for dish wares. So far, no operational issues and really enjoying the quiet. We hope this one will last as long as the one it replaced.

Sentence (English): Bought to replace an old Series 6.
Comments (English): [ Not bad, but could be much better ] || ---------------- || Bought to replace an old Series 6. Key consideration was the automatic door opening. have to say I am disappointed. the door doesn't actually open until the very end of the cycle, and releases very little steam. so there is still a lot of condensation on items inside the dishwasher. Only a marginal improvement over the old one in this regard. The top tray also only cleans from the top - ie if the "middle" tray is full, there is no way for water to get to the bottom of the top tray. this is a design flaw in most of the dishwashers i looked at. WiFi / smart home features are handy, and plenty of space and adjustable trays / storage etc. Overall pretty good, but a software upgrade to open the door early after the wash cycle has finished, to actually let all the steam out, would be a massive improvement.

Sentence (English): Purchased this DW after a four year old Whirlpool went kaput for the 2nd time in a year. (
Comments (English): [ Very pleased! ] || ---------------- || Purchased this DW after a four year old Whirlpool went kaput for the 2nd time in a year. (Whirlpool sent someone to replace the motor unit free of charge, then less than one year later, the same problem occurred.) Time for a Maytag! - which we hope will live up to Maytag's long standing reputation of reliability. I installed the unit myself. It is very quiet and does an excellent job when loaded as suggested by the mfg. The stainless tub is great. (No funky plastic odor! ) The silverware rack on top is wonderful. We haven't even used the other silverware rack yet. Operation time varies. We usually choose the 2:43 cycle. There's a shorter cycle option and a longer cycle that takes around 3.5 hours. We were used to a faster wash cycle with our old unit, however the dishes and silverware never came this clean, so there is no complaint about how long it takes. Just had to adjust our lifestyle and expectations a little. Very pleased after daily use for the last ten or so days. One thing you should be aware of is that the main racks are set lower than the old school units we've had over the years. This means more overall space and a third rack on top for silverware, but if you have issues with bending, you might want to check out the floor model in the store to see if it's right for you before purchasing.

Reason for Purchase: * I purchased this when moving into a new apartment. Energy Efficiency: As a product that has achieved Energy Efficiency Grade 1, it maintains powerful performance while reducing power consumption thanks to Smart Inverter technology. Cleaning: It thoroughly removes rice grains and grease, and when used with dedicated detergent, you can use your dishes cleanly without any residue. 2. Design: The minimalist and sophisticated design of the LG Objet Collection blends harmoniously with your kitchen interior. Its excellent integration with other kitchen appliances contributes to high customer satisfaction. 3. Easy Maintenance: The automatic door opening function allows for natural drying after washing, ensuring a clean finish without water stains. 4. Diverse Wash Modes: It offers high practicality by allowing you to select the appropriate mode for your needs, ranging from small loads to large loads. It operates efficiently, especially when washing a small number of dishes. 5. Water and Electricity Savings: The savings on water and electricity bills are particularly attractive to users. There are even reviews stating that water bills have decreased compared to before thanks to the automatic power consumption control feature. Other: Installation proceeds quickly, and a professional technician neatly organizes the space to fit.
